chunks: What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from Abī Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a غلام whom I brought with me, and I instructed him, so he performed tamattuʿ, then he entered into hajj on the Day of al-Tarwiyah, and I did not slaughter on his behalf. Does he have the option to fast after the departure, when the days which Allah, Exalted is He, mentioned have already passed?
So he said: Why did you not instruct him to perform hajj separately (ifrād)? I said: I sought the good.
He said: Since you sought the good, then go and slaughter on his behalf a fat sheep. And that was on the final day of departure.

key_terms.أَهَلَّ بِالْحَجِّ: he entered into the state and declaration of hajj
key_terms.شَاةً سَمِينَةً: a fat sheep to be offered as sacrifice
key_terms.غُلَامٍ: a young male servant or slave in this legal context
key_terms.يَصُومَ: to fast as a substitute in a ritual legal context
key_terms.يَوْمَ التَّرْوِيَةِ: the eighth day of Dhu al-Ḥijjah
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّفْرِ الْأَخِيرِ: the final day of departure from Minā

ai.seo_question: If a slave performs hajj al-tamattuʿ with his master's permission and no sacrificial animal is slaughtered, can he fast after the days have passed?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of a غلام who performed hajj al-tamattuʿ with his master's permission, while the sacrificial offering had not been slaughtered on his behalf within its proper time. The Imam عليه السلام directs the master to provide a sheep instead of relying on fasting after the designated days have passed, indicating the master's responsibility in this case.
